note: Example parity policy for a project that is developed in one checkout and published from another. Copy it to configs/tree_parity.json (gitignored by convention in the tree that holds the real paths), fill in the two roots, then run `make parity POLICY=configs/tree_parity.json`. Every may-differ entry needs a reason: an exception without one is reported as drift regardless of the paths involved. Anything that differs and is covered by no rule at all is reported as unclassified drift, so a new file cannot be added to one checkout and forgotten in the other.

may_differ.loopgate/gates/private_tool.py: development-only tooling that is not published
may_differ.configs/*: the development tree names real targets; the published tree carries sanitized ones
may_differ.README.md: the published README is rewritten for strangers
